label: The Arnold Conjecture
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 417 to 456 and centers on a single bold claim of Arnold: a Hamiltonian symplectomorphism of a closed manifold must have at least as many fixed points as a smooth function has critical points. We open by framing that count as a topological lower bound rather than an accident of dynamics.

label: From Functions to Fixed Points
notes: Morse theory says any function on a closed manifold has critical points bounded below by the sum of Betti numbers. Arnold's insight transports this counting principle from gradients of functions to fixed points of Hamiltonian maps, asserting the same homological floor governs symplectic dynamics.

label: Statement of the Conjecture
notes: We state the conjecture precisely: the number of fixed points of a Hamiltonian symplectomorphism is at least the sum of Betti numbers in the nondegenerate case. The degenerate cup-length bound is weaker but holds more generally, paralleling the two classical Morse lower bounds for functions.

label: The Torus Model
notes: The torus gives the cleanest finite shadow of the conjecture. A height-style Morse function on the two-torus has one minimum, two saddles, and one maximum, four critical points matching the Betti sum one, two, one. This is the executable check carried by the notebook for this chapter.

label: Morse Inequalities
notes: The Morse inequalities relate the number of critical points of index k to the Betti numbers, with the strong form bounding alternating sums. These inequalities are the precise mechanism that converts homology into a count, and Floer homology will reproduce them in infinite dimensions.

label: The Symplectic Action Functional
notes: On the free loop space we define the symplectic action, a functional whose critical points are exactly the one-periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow. Those orbits correspond to fixed points of the time-one map, recasting a dynamical counting problem as Morse theory on an infinite-dimensional space.

label: Action on the Loop Space
notes: We picture the action as a landscape over the loop space. Its critical points are the constant or periodic loops where the gradient vanishes, and the Morse picture suggests that homology of the loop space should bound their number, even though the functional is unbounded above and below.

label: The Conley-Zehnder Index
notes: Because the action is neither bounded nor of finite index, ordinary Morse index fails. The Conley-Zehnder index assigns each nondegenerate periodic orbit an integer from the path of symplectic matrices its linearization traces, providing the grading that replaces the Morse index in Floer's construction.

label: Lagrangian Intersections
notes: The conjecture has a Lagrangian form: a closed Lagrangian submanifold and its image under a Hamiltonian isotopy must intersect in at least the number of critical points a function on the Lagrangian requires. Intersection points play the role fixed points did in the fixed-point version.

label: Forcing Intersections
notes: We visualize a Lagrangian and its Hamiltonian image. Energy considerations and the exactness of the displacement prevent the image from being pushed entirely off the original, forcing intersections that cannot be removed by isotopy. Counting these points is the geometric heart of the Lagrangian conjecture.

label: Floer Homology Overview
notes: Floer homology realizes the loop-space Morse theory rigorously. Generators are periodic orbits graded by Conley-Zehnder index, the differential counts J-holomorphic cylinders between orbits, and the resulting homology equals the singular homology of the manifold, which yields the Betti-number lower bound Arnold predicted.

label: Synthesis and Outlook
notes: We close by tracing the full arc: functions to fixed points, fixed points to action critical points, action to Floer homology. The chapter establishes the conjecture in major cases and sets up later refinements, displacement energy, and the Lagrangian Floer theory developed in the following chapters.
